113.form: Signed multipart lead. The narrow authorization, common process minimum, and purpose-duration limitation have different direct majority coalitions. The additional evidentiary-presumption and initial military-tribunal permissions have only three joins and remain an expressly identified plurality part. A single member of that three-Justice group can carry every part; splitting authors is unnecessary. Separate writings preserve the Chief's distinct burden, the statutory objection, the release/prosecution alternative, and executive deference.
113.compat: The Chief joins narrow statutory authorization, the severable common process minimum, and the purpose-duration limitation. His approved clear-and-convincing government burden is neither abandoned nor attributed to colleagues: it appears in his separate writing. O'Connor, Kennedy and Breyer supply all four lead parts; Souter and Ginsburg join only the common process and conditional purpose-duration parts, retaining their statutory objection and express proof/habeas barriers. Thomas joins only the bare narrow authorizing proposition, not the full purpose-duration rule, and dissents from the remand. Stevens and Scalia reject the status-hearing remedy itself. No post-reconciliation commitment changed. All six remand votes support meaningful adjudication, not a common complete proof rule. No Marks aggregation can turn the inconsistent proof allocations into a controlling quantum. No fallback is used.

116.form: Signed merits opinion applying two distinct statutory and constitutional inquiries to the reviewed appellate grant. The plenary merits posture and substantial explanation of record-development predicates justify a signed lead; historical summary form does not determine present form. All nine support the full governing rationale. The separate disposition-form reconciliation confirms reversal and remand on those unchanged grounds; no author selected.
116.compat: The supplemental Stone-free Holland disposition-form reconciliation confirms that all eight Associates support reversal and remand on the precise unchanged J1 grounds. The Chief supports the same action and distinct inquiries, producing a unanimous reversal and remand. No statutory trigger, exception, prejudice standard or ultimate factual finding changes. Historical review-denial preferences remain distinct from present merits support. No standing fallback is used.

114.form: Signed lead with a five-Justice objective effectiveness rule and a severable six-Justice application to the proved deliberate, uncured method. Kennedy joins the application only and gives his different general trigger separately. The three ordinary-Elstad-remand votes dissent. A single supporter of the objective rule can write all lead portions.
114.compat: The Chief's objective complete-sequence rule adds a fifth direct S1 join. His proposed warning-and-waiver showing includes the ordinary preponderance standard; the draft states that as the ordinary applicable prosecution burden, not a new proof rule inferred from a general outcome. The record's deliberately coordinated technique also supplies the six-Justice sufficient application S2, but Kennedy does not join intent-independent S1. Breyer retains his independent fruits/good-faith proposal. O'Connor, Scalia and Thomas retain vacatur for ordinary Elstad inquiry, never automatic admission. No commitment change or fallback is used.

112.form: Signed two-component lead with a seven-Justice base-specific habeas rationale preserving Eisentrager and a civil branch distinguishing universal litigation disability from each legal predicate. Scalia and Thomas join the severable rejection of universal alien incapacity and independent-statutory remand, while opposing habeas and the constitutional-dependent civil disposition. One author can carry all majority propositions; Kennedy's documented rationale barrier is honored directly.
112.compat: The Chief joins the base-specific statutory rationale, not a universal foreign-custody constitutional holding. Kennedy joins that complete rationale because Eisentrager is distinguished on enduring control and absence of military adjudication, and Braden is used only to reject an invariable physical-presence requirement; no destruction of Eisentrager's statutory foundation is asserted. This matches R1-K without changing a frozen ground. The civil judgment has seven full-remand votes and two limited remands. Scalia and Thomas retain affirmance of constitutional-dependent theories; their severable statutory and alien-incapacity joins supply no general entitlement. The supplemental Stone-free civil-form reconciliation confirms six Associates support reversal of the complete civil dismissal and Scalia and Thomas support reversal only of the genuinely independent statutory branch, while affirming the constitutional-dependent branch. These formal clarifications preserve all frozen grounds and the existing historical-departure explanations. No fallback is used.

111.form: Signed lead deciding the ordinary domestic immediate-custodian and forum rules and the conditional transfer remedy. A separate concurrence preserves O'Connor and Kennedy's personal-jurisdiction/venue characterization, waiver and supported-evasion exceptions. Four dissenters reach a confined exceptional-control theory and detention merits. One author can carry all majority propositions.
111.compat: The Chief, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas share P1 and P-T. The transfer direction requires consideration and use only when a real statutory route and its predicates exist; it finds no §1631 eligibility. O'Connor and Kennedy expressly preserve their personal/venue characterization, waiver and obstruction exceptions in a concurrence. Neither Scalia nor Thomas receives a detention-merits vote. Stevens, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer retain the exceptional directing-custodian theory and confined no-authority merits ground. No bad faith is found. No changed commitment or fallback.

115.form: Signed narrow-remedy Court opinion. The full five share the physical-fruit rule; the broader constitutional duty/deterrence theory is a separate two-Justice concurrence, not part of the lead. Three affirmance dissenters and Breyer's different good-faith-remand dissent remain distinct. One full-rationale supporter can carry the entire lead.
115.compat: The Chief supplies Pt-G's fifth direct join. He preserves the constitutional warning duty, differentiated evidence remedies, actual-coercion distinction and independent acquisition objections. O'Connor and Kennedy join only the narrow remedy, consistent with their express refusal to adopt Pt-duty. Scalia and Thomas can fully join the narrower remedy without requiring their additional theory in it. Stevens, Souter and Ginsburg affirm suppression under Pt-F; Breyer instead requires a good-faith finding and supplies neither unconditional affirmance nor a fifth admission vote. No officer-intent finding or complete waiver is inferred. The existing appellate probable-cause rejection is preserved. No fallback is used.
